segments.he: אמר הכותב באשר הי' ד' עמדי וזיכני ברחמיו הגדולים בשנה הזאת להיות "בארץ ישראל" ולהסתפח קצת בנחלת ד.ך באדמת קודש. וידעתי עם לבבי כי הכל רק בכחו וזכותו של רבינו הק' אור האורות וכו' כמהור"ר נחמן זצוק"ל בעל המחבר ספרי לקוטי מוהר"ן וסיפורי מעשיות ושאר ספרים הק'. כי הוא גילה לנו במאמריו ז"ל גודל נפלאות מעלת קדושת "ארץ ישראל" גם עכשיו כשהוא בגלות וכו'. וגודל החיוב כמעט כל כל אחד מישראל להיות "בא"י" לפי שעה על כל פנים אם אי אפשר לו להשתקע שם ולדור שם בקביעות. וכמו שאמר בפירוש בהתחלת מאמר ט' תיקונין. שמי שרוצה להיות איש ישראל דהיינו שילך בכל פעם מדרגא לדרגא בעבודת ד' אי אפשר לו אלא ע"י "ארץ ישראל" וכו'. וכמבואר במקום אחר. גם גילה דעתו כמה פעמים על ענין השגתו הנפלאה והנוראה שיש אצלו הבדל והפרש גדול מאד בין ההשגה שקודם "א"י" ובין ההשגה שזכה אח"כ אחר היותו "בא"י". וכל דבריו הנדפסים בספריו הם מההשגות שהשיג אחר "א"י". Translator's Preface: This is a complete, word-for-word translation of Zimras HaAretz, following the guidelines of faithful formal equivalence. Every word of the Hebrew is rendered. Verses are italicized with source citations. Key Kabbalistic and Chassidic terms are transliterated in Ashkenazic pronunciation and explained in brackets on first occurrence. The Hebrew vowel tzairai is rendered ai/ay. Parenthetical passages in the original are translated in full, marked with the original parentheses.
 

This installment covers: the full Introduction (Hakdamah) and Simanim 1–5 of Likutay Kama.

 Introduction — Hakdamah

Introduction.

segments.he: ודברי אלו המועטין שבחיבור הקטן הזה הם תועלת גדול גם ליושבי חוץ לארץ להעלות על לבם תמיד זכרון קדושת "ארץ ישראל וירושלים". ולהיות להם כיסופים וגעגועים חזקים בכל פעם לבוא לשם לפי שעה על כל פנים. ואולי יזכו לקבוע דירתם שם בתמידות ולהשתוקק שם ג"כ לאיזו הארה והתנוצצות קודש מבחי' קדושת "ארץ ישראל" אשר אין ערוך לקדושתה כלל מארחר שהיא כלליות הכל כנ"ל. אך ליושבי "א"י" מסוגל ביותר לעיין בזה. כי כמעט שלא נמצא ענין אחד מהמצטרך שם שלא יהיה מבואר בחיבור קטן זה. בפרט שכל הדברים שבחיבור זה יסודתם בהררי קודש. היינו. על דברי רבינו הק' זצוק"ל. אשר כל דיבור ודיבור מדבריו ז"ל הם מקצוע גדול בתורה. ויכולים להרחיב הדיבור בהם עד אין סוף ואין תכלית והם עיקר גדול לעבודת ד' וכמבואר במקום אחר מזה קצת:
segments.en:
The author declares: Inasmuch as Hashem was with me, and He merited me — in His great mercies — in this year to be "in Eretz Yisrael" and to be absorbed somewhat into the inheritance of Hashem upon holy soil — I knew within my heart that all of this was only through the power and the merit of our holy Rabbainu, the Light of Lights, etc., the Master Rabbi Nachman, may his holy and righteous memory be a blessing, [zatzukl — an acronym: may the memory of the holy and righteous one be for a blessing], the author of the books Likutay Moharan, Sipuray Maasiyos [Story-Tales], and the other holy books. For it is he who revealed to us in his teachings, of blessed memory, the tremendous wondrous greatness of the elevation of the sanctity of "Eretz Yisrael" even now while it is in exile, etc. And the great obligation — upon virtually every single individual of Israel — to be "in Eretz Yisrael" at least temporarily in any case, even if it is impossible for him to settle and dwell there permanently.

And as he stated explicitly at the beginning of the teaching of the Nine Tikkunim [rectifications]: that whoever wishes to be a true Ish Yisrael [a man of Israel] — meaning, that he should go each time from level to level in the service of Hashem — this is impossible for him except through "Eretz Yisrael", etc. And as is explained elsewhere.

He also revealed his view many times regarding the matter of his wondrous and awesome hasagah [attainment / spiritual comprehension] — that there is within him a very great difference and distinction between the comprehension that was before "Eretz Yisrael", and the comprehension that he merited afterwards, after being "in Eretz Yisrael." And all of his words printed in his books come from the comprehensions he attained after "Eretz Yisrael." (With the exception of a few minor teachings, as explained elsewhere.)

Therefore I set my heart to record — in outline-form and brief allusion — how all of his teachings, of blessed memory, have a great connection to the matter of the sanctity of "Eretz Yisrael", and how the sanctity of "Eretz Yisrael" is included within all the wondrous matters explained in his teachings, of blessed memory. For "Eretz Yisrael" is the totality of all the holiness within all the holinesses — as explained in Likutay Moharan (Siman 234).

segments.he: והנה החיבור הזה מיוסד על מאמרים הק' שבספרי ליקוטי מוהר"ן הראשון הושני ועל המעשיות שנדפסו בספר סיפורי מעשיות וקצת מהשיחות שאחר הסיפורי מעשיות. ואם ירצה המעיין לעמוד על שרשי הדבירם ולהתבונן בהם כראוי. אזי יעיין בפנים הספרים הק' הנ"ל ואחר כך יעיין בחיבור זה בכל סימן וסי' כפי המצוין עליו. וקראתי שם זה החיבור הקטן זמרת הארץ "שתרגומו" דמשבח בארעא. כי מדובר בו אך ורק משבחי "ארץ ישראל". ואיך "שא"י" היא כלליות הקדושה ואין שום דבר קדוש בעולם הן בדעות הן במדות וכיוצא בזה שלא יהי' כלול בקדושת "ארץ ישראל" כנ"ל:
segments.en:
Now in some places I have brought a support and proof for the general sanctity of "Eretz Yisrael" from a single verse or from a teaching of our Sages of blessed memory that speaks solely of "Tzion and Yerushalayim and the Bais HaMikdash." But in truth, all is one — for all the Ten Sanctities "of Eretz Yisrael" receive from one another and are included within one another. From the Holy of Holies, illumination flows to the entire Bais HaMikdash [Holy Temple]; and from there to the entire city of "Tzion and Yerushalayim"; and from there to all the cities of Yehudah and Yisrael "in Eretz Yisrael."

And I have supported myself on the teaching of the holy Zohar (Bereishis 114): "All those who remain in the holy land of Israel — their judgment is as Yerushalayim and as Tzion in every matter," etc. And our Rabbis of blessed memory said: "In the future, Yerushalayim will spread across all of Eretz Yisrael," etc.

And these few words of mine in this small composition are of great benefit even to those who dwell outside the Land — to raise up in their hearts always the remembrance of the sanctity of "Eretz Yisrael and Yerushalayim," and to have strong kisufim [longings] and ga'agu'im [yearnings] each time to come there — at least temporarily in any case. And perhaps they will merit to establish their dwelling there permanently, and to yearn there as well for some illumination and holy sparkling of the aspect of the sanctity of "Eretz Yisrael" — whose sanctity is entirely beyond measure, since it is the totality of everything, as stated above.

However, for those who dwell in "Eretz Yisrael" this is most suited — for there is virtually not a single matter from those that are needed there that will not be explained in this small composition. Particularly because all the matters in this composition are founded upon mountains of holiness — namely, upon the words of our holy Rabbainu, may his holy and righteous memory be for a blessing — for every single utterance of his words, of blessed memory, is a great domain in Torah. And one can expand upon them endlessly and infinitely, and they are a great essential foundation for the service of Hashem, as is explained elsewhere regarding this somewhat.

And behold, this composition is founded upon the holy ma'amarim [teachings] in the books of Likutay Moharan, the first and the second, and upon the Story-Tales printed in the book Sipuray Maasiyos, and some of the conversations that follow the Story-Tales. And if the reader wishes to grasp the roots of these matters and contemplate them as is fitting, let him then study the aforementioned holy books themselves, and afterwards study this composition — each siman [section] according to what is indicated upon it.

And I have called the name of this small composition Zimras HaAretz — "whose translation" [Aramaic rendering] is d'meshabe'ach b'ar'a "that praises the land" — for it speaks solely and exclusively of the praises of "Eretz Yisrael," and how "Eretz Yisrael" is the totality of holiness, and there is no holy matter in the world — whether in the realm of de'os [knowledge / ideas], or midos [character traits], or anything similar — that is not included in the sanctity of "Eretz Yisrael," as stated above.

 לִקּוּטֵי קַמָּא

aligned_segments.he: ואיך "שא"י" היא כלליות הקדושה ואין שום דבר קדוש בעולם הן בדעות הן במדות וכיוצא בזה שלא יהי' כלול בקדושת "ארץ ישראל" כנ"ל:
aligned_segments.en:
And if the reader wishes to grasp the roots of these matters and contemplate them as is fitting, let him then study the aforementioned holy books themselves, and afterwards study this composition — each siman [section] according to what is indicated upon it. And I have called the name of this small composition Zimras HaAretz — "whose translation" [Aramaic rendering] is d'meshabe'ach b'ar'a "that praises the land" — for it speaks solely and exclusively of the praises of "Eretz Yisrael," and how "Eretz Yisrael" is the totality of holiness, and there is no holy matter in the world — whether in the realm of de'os [knowledge / ideas], or midos [character traits], or anything similar — that is not included in the sanctity of "Eretz Yisrael," as stated above.

 לִקּוּטֵי קַמָּא

 Likutay Kama — Part One
